main_body: A flat seamless grass ground patch (64x48 px) of one mid green with sparse dark and light dot clusters; terrain tile with no standing volume
top_band: none (flat ground texture; the column scan shows only mid green L=113 with occasional 1-row L=136 dots)
evidence: Terrain ground tile, not a standing object. It has no top or front face, and the 3/4 contract does not apply. Ground is drawn as a flat surface, which is correct for the kind, with no side faces and no elevation. Pass for Part A because the kind is flat terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours in total, against 80 for the reference grass, and a median of 4 colours per tile against 26 for the grass reference. The main grass ramp has only about 2-3 steps (mid green plus a lighter dot and a darker clump), whereas Beodeul grass uses 5 or more greens with clumps and tufts. The texture is a regular, repeating motif (checker clusters, dark blobs, single dots) tiled every 16 px, so it reads as a mechanical pattern rather than hand-shaded grass. Large areas of one flat mid green between the dots (7% flat-fill coverage, higher than the 0% of both references) add to the shallow look. There are no outlines, which is fine for ground. Overall it is clearly thinner and flatter than the grass reference.
